title: Maintenance Escalation, Safe Boundaries & Reconstructable Handoff

content.overview: A specialist handoff should narrow the problem and preserve evidence without crossing into unauthorized electrical, controls or protected calibration work.

vocabulary.definition: A structured transfer of verified fault evidence to the role authorized to service the equipment.
The limit of checks a worker may perform without entering protected servicing or hazardous-energy work.
A record another qualified person can use to understand what happened, what was checked and what remains unresolved.

sections.title: Name the device and event
sections.body: Include device/system ID, affected zone, time, alarm/command history, verified sensor evidence and crop/process consequence.

sections.title: Document checks already completed
sections.body: State colocated comparisons, reference checks, placement review or safe resets already performed so qualified maintenance does not repeat or misinterpret the earlier work.

sections.title: Do not cross into protected servicing
sections.body: Opening energized panels, bypassing safeguards or performing unqualified calibration/repair is outside the educational scope and should be escalated.

workedExamples: A useful escalation states that Unit DH-2 received three commands, showed no expected status change, canopy RH increased and sensor agreement was verified; it does not instruct an unqualified worker to open the unit.
commonMistakes: Crossing into protected repair because the probable fault seems obvious.
content.practicalApplication: Write a maintenance/controls escalation from a supplied alarm and sensor log.
content.summary: Good escalation turns raw alarms into actionable evidence while preserving safety and authority boundaries.
